items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Mattie Hite was added, and there were 12 chorus girls, with the comedy being handled by George Williams and Galli de Gaston, two favourites of Harlem.

ctx.x: raise. I can't remember what was his reason exactly, but perhaps he thought he could arrange things when we returned to New York, and he would have a face to face talk with the directors of the circuit. But nothing happened.

The band did not break up, however, and we continued to do theaters that were not run by R.K.O. We played the Lafayette, the Mount Morris, a theater on 125th Street and 5th Avenue, went on a tour of upstate New York playing Glen Falls at the Empire, the Playhouse in Johnstown, and a theater in Syracuse. Mattie Hite was added, and there were 12 chorus girls, with the comedy being handled by George Williams and Galli de Gaston, two favourites of Harlem.

The tour ended in November and so did the Ralph Cooper orchestra because no more bookings were coming in. Living with Madeline had also become so unbearable that we separated for the third and last time. Grandma Jackson and her family had left Springfield and moved to New York three years before I separated from my wife. Dickie Wells was staying with Grandma and I took a room with her also.
